title: The Grunion Run, xxii
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Twenty-second year. Nine lanterns. The run barely a run. Gully's girl, nine, asks why there used to be more. Wood says the fish moved. Gully says the people did.

panels.composition: The beach, nine lanterns. A thin line at the surf. GULLY's thermos. The girl with a bucket. WOOD. BARNABY II.

image.prompt: a night beach with only nine lanterns and a thin line of people at the surf, a man with a thermos, a girl with a bucket, a thin man with a pad, a three-legged dog, clean ink with a muted wash

panels.composition: The girl, looking down the beach at the dark where lanterns used to be.

balloons.text: Dad said there used to be a hundred.

image.prompt: a small girl looking down a dark beach, two men answering her differently

panels.composition: Wood and Gully. A look. Both right.

image.prompt: close-up of two men exchanging a look, both right, no words

panels.composition: Silent. Nine lanterns. The fish, few. The pup, the girl, the bucket. Wood drawing this one — the first Grunion Run he draws instead of watches in years.

image.prompt: silent wide night beach panel with nine lanterns and a few silver fish, a girl with a bucket and a three-legged dog at the surf, a man drawing, no words
image.notes: Pad open. He draws this one because it's ending.

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust

notes: Nine lanterns. 'The fish moved.' 'The people did.' He draws it.
